findings.quote: The decision to sell was made
findings.note: The action verb "sell" is buried in the noun "decision", while the clause is carried by the empty verb "was made".
The verb "evaluate" is buried in the noun "evaluation", which is carried by the empty verb "carried out".
"Realization" names the act of realizing, and the clause's verb is the empty "had come to." The action is buried in the noun.
The draft does not say who should note this. The surrounding sentences give the author's own views, so the reader can infer the author, but only with effort.
Three consecutive sentences open with "I" followed by a past-tense verb: "I left", "I reached", "I arrived".

findings.quote: After eleven years of sitting in morning traffic behind a school bus, I
findings.note: The main subject 'I' arrives after eighteen words of introductory material.
"It should be noted that" is a stock phrase that delays the content without adding meaning.
"very" is an intensifier that adds emphasis without changing the claim that the winter was hard.
"basically" is an empty hedge that weakens the claim it modifies.
"Insurance" repeats the word first used in "My insurance renewal" two sentences earlier.
"picturesque" repeats in the next sentence after "I pass a picturesque row of Victorian houses on Linden Street."

findings.quote: A monthly bus pass costs sixty.
findings.note: The previous sentence is about the yearly cost of insurance, parking, fuel and repairs. This sentence opens on a monthly bus pass, new at the opening; the comparison only surfaces at the figure at the end.

findings.quote: Many people live too far from work
findings.note: The previous sentence was about differing situations and what works for one person. This sentence opens on a new element, many people, with no shared term linking back.

findings.quote: I can only describe what happened to me, in my own circumstances, which may or may not resemble yours.
findings.note: Restatement. It repeats the earlier point "Everyone's situation is different, and what works for one person will not necessarily work for another" plus the point that the writer is only describing his own case.

findings.quote: It should be noted that I am not trying to tell anyone else how to live.
findings.note: Throat-clearing. It announces the disclaimer that the following sentences then state directly.
The noun "determination" buries the verb "determine", with "makes" doing the work.
"conduct" is an empty verb carrying the action noun "review"; the verb "review" itself is available.
The clause hides who made the decision to route all changes through the board. The surrounding sentences describe the process but never name the deciding party.
The draft does not say who raised the concerns. The next sentence names the author and the board, but not the person or group raising concerns.
"The board" opens three consecutive sentences, and the same construction repeats in a fourth.

"Clearly" asserts obviousness the text has not established.

findings.quote: The median wait for approval fell from six days to nineteen hours.

findings.quote: A change finished on a Friday therefore waits six days.

findings.quote: It was decided in 2023 that all changes would go through this process,
findings.note: The sentence opens on an unnamed decision-making event in 2023, which nothing earlier in the paragraph introduces. The previous sentence concerned the six-day wait for a Friday change.

The previous sentence concerns the board's checklist and weekly schedule, while this one opens on unnamed concerns raised by unnamed parties. Nothing earlier has introduced these concerns or their raisers.
The previous sentence was about leads recording approvals in the release ticket; admission controllers appear here with nothing earlier preparing them.

findings.quote: a toll booth on the highway to production
findings.note: Stock image doing the work of an argument. The draft never says what the toll is, who collects it, or what the highway stands for, so the comparison supplies a feeling of obstruction rather than a mechanism.

findings.quote: A safety net should catch mistakes without becoming a straitjacket
findings.note: Mixed figure: the safety net and the straitjacket are two incompatible images in one sentence, and the straitjacket's literal claim about constraint is never spelled out.
Restatement: the sentence only repeats the result already given, that both teams cut their median wait from six days to under one and neither shipped a change that had to be rolled back.

findings.quote: Oversight would remain in place for the changes where it matters most, and that point should not be lost.
findings.note: Restatement: the sentence repeats the point already made in nothing in this proposal would change that.
The noun "undertaking" carries the act of committing, while the verb "given" supplies only the tense. The real action survives as the noun.
The noun "assessment" holds the assessing, and the verb "carry out" does none of the work. The actor is separated from the action by two stacked nouns.
The noun "decision" conceals the act of deciding, carried by the empty verb "made".

The draft does not say who promised the sandbags, though the next sentence's reference to the council is the only nearby candidate. The actor is the party accountable for a failure the paragraph is about.
